selinux.finding: not present -- SELinux is not installed on this OS choice (Ubuntu). This is not a misconfiguration, it's a different LSM choice.

fips.finding: FIPS mode not applicable -- standard Ubuntu kernel has no FIPS module

ssh.finding: password authentication is ENABLED for this host -- a hardened baseline would typically be key-only

host_firewall.finding: no host-level firewall active -- network policy enforcement for cluster traffic is via Cilium (infrastructure/cilium/), not a host firewall on appserv itself

resilience-lab-controlplane-1.reason: Talos nodes have no SSH and no shell at all -- there is no remote-exec mechanism to run a script against them, by design, not by omission. talosctl's own gRPC API (the only management surface) was not reachable from this session (endpoint config issue, tracked separately) -- even when reachable, it exposes structured resources, not a shell to run checks in.

architectural_facts.lsm: No traditional LSM (no SELinux, no AppArmor) -- Talos has no policy-based access control layer at all.
architectural_facts.hardening_model: Structural rather than policy-based: a signed, read-only, immutable root filesystem; no package manager; no shell; the only management surface is an authenticated gRPC API (talosctl). A host with no shell and no writable root filesystem has a categorically smaller attack surface than a conventional Linux box, even without SELinux/AppArmor/FIPS in the traditional sense.
architectural_facts.source: https://www.talos.dev/latest/introduction/security-disclosure-process/ and Talos's own architecture documentation -- this is Talos's documented design, not this project's own claim.
